questions.q: Which two rivers meet at Belgrade?
questions.fact: The confluence of the Sava and the Danube is the view from Kalemegdan, the fortress whose walls run from Roman to Austrian times.

questions.q: You land at Nikola Tesla Airport. What does bus 72 into the centre cost?
options: A ticket bought in an app
questions.fact: Since 1 January 2025 all regular Belgrade city public transport has been free, the airport buses included. Fare policies change, so check before you rely on it.

questions.q: Can you pay cash in euros in Belgrade?
options: Not really: the dinar is the only legal cash currency
Yes, euros are legal tender everywhere
questions.fact: Many prices are quoted in euros, but you pay the dinar equivalent. The few places that take euro notes informally usually give a poor rate.

questions.q: Every foreign visitor's address must be registered with the police. Within how long of arrival?
questions.fact: The 24-hour rule applies to every nationality. Hotels usually do it at check-in and hand you a white card; in a private apartment the host must register you, or you do it yourself.

questions.q: A friend suggests a night on a splav. What are you getting into?
options: A bar, restaurant or club floating on the river
questions.fact: Splav simply means a floating structure tied to the bank. On the Sava and the Danube it covers everything from quiet riverside bars to big nightclubs.

questions.q: What do Belgraders call Ada Ciganlija?
questions.fact: It's a lake and beach peninsula on the Sava with swimming, cafés and sports, and lifeguards from May to September.

questions.q: What does the golden orb at the Nikola Tesla Museum hold?
questions.fact: The museum holds Tesla's personal archive and runs live electrical demonstrations. Bring dinars: it's cash only.

questions.q: Why do Zemun's streets feel so different from central Belgrade?
options: For centuries it was the Habsburg frontier town facing Ottoman Belgrade
It was rebuilt as a Venetian port
It was the capital of Yugoslavia
It was built for the 1970s Olympics bid
questions.fact: That border history is why Zemun is lower, older and more Central European, with a fish-restaurant quay and the Gardoš Tower above the Danube.

questions.q: What is the theme of Expo 2027 Belgrade?
options: Play for Humanity: Sport and Music for All
Designing Future Society for Our Lives
Feeding the Planet, Energy for Life
questions.fact: The wrong answers belong to Dubai 2020, Osaka 2025 and Milan 2015. Belgrade's Expo runs from 15 May to 15 August 2027 at Surčin.

questions.q: How many countries has the organiser said are registered for Expo 2027?
questions.fact: The director called it a record for a Specialised Expo. Our tracker follows every country that has been publicly named.
